name: Digital multimeter
purpose: Measures voltage, current and resistance in electrical circuits. Use the correct input socket, function and range before connecting the probes.

parts.label: Display
parts.info: Shows the measured value, unit and status symbols.

parts.label: Function dial
parts.info: Selects the measurement function and range.

parts.label: Voltage / resistance socket
parts.info: Commonly accepts the black COM lead and red voltage/resistance lead.

parts.label: Current socket
parts.info: Dedicated current input; use only within the meter's marked rating and fuse limits.

parts.label: Test probes
parts.info: Insulated leads used to make contact with the test points.

steps.title: Inspect the meter and leads
steps.text: Check the case, display, probe insulation and probe tips for cracks, exposed metal or damage. Do not use damaged equipment.
steps.warning: Never use a meter or lead with damaged insulation, a cracked case or an exposed conductor.

steps.title: Connect the leads correctly
steps.text: With the circuit de-energized, insert the black lead into COM. Insert the red lead into the voltage/resistance socket for voltage or resistance measurements. Use a current socket only for a current measurement and only after checking the meter rating.
steps.warning: A lead left in the current socket can create a short circuit if used for a voltage measurement. Verify the socket before every connection.

steps.title: Select the measurement function
steps.text: Turn the function dial to the required quantity: voltage, resistance or current. Select AC or DC as appropriate. If the meter is not auto-ranging, begin at a range higher than the expected value.

steps.title: Connect to the test points
steps.text: For voltage, connect the probes in parallel across the component or supply. For resistance, switch off and isolate power and discharge capacitors before measuring. For current, the meter must be inserted in series by a person trained for the circuit.
steps.warning: Never measure resistance on an energized circuit. Never place a meter in current mode directly across a voltage source.

steps.title: Read and record the result
steps.text: Keep fingers behind the probe guards. Read the value and unit on the display. If the display shows overload, an unexpected value or unstable readings, stop and check the range, connections and circuit condition.

steps.title: Disconnect and store safely
steps.text: Remove the probes from the circuit. Turn the dial to OFF. Return the red lead to the voltage socket if appropriate for storage, coil the leads without sharp bends and store the meter dry.

quiz.q: Where is the black test lead normally connected?
quiz.why: The black lead normally connects to the common (COM) socket.

quiz.q: What must be done before measuring resistance?
options: Move the red lead to the current socket
quiz.why: Resistance measurements must be made on a de-energized, isolated circuit; capacitors may also need discharging.

quiz.q: How is voltage measured across a component?
quiz.why: Voltage is the potential difference between two points, so probes are placed in parallel.

quiz.q: What can happen if current mode is connected directly across a voltage source?
quiz.why: Current mode has a low-resistance path and must be inserted in series, not placed across a source.

name: Compound microscope
purpose: Uses objective and eyepiece lenses to magnify small specimens for observation. Begin with the lowest-power objective and focus gently.

parts.label: Eyepiece
parts.info: Lens viewed through; commonly provides 10× magnification.

parts.label: Objective lenses
parts.info: Selectable lenses near the specimen that provide different magnifications.

parts.label: Stage
parts.info: Platform that supports the slide; clips or a mechanical holder secure it.

parts.label: Coarse focus knob
parts.info: Moves the stage or body tube through a larger distance for initial focus.

parts.label: Fine focus knob
parts.info: Makes small adjustments to sharpen the image.

parts.label: Illuminator
parts.info: Provides light through or onto the specimen.

steps.title: Carry and position the microscope
steps.text: Carry the microscope upright with one hand supporting the arm and the other supporting the base. Place it on a stable, dry bench away from the edge.
steps.warning: Do not carry a microscope by its eyepiece, stage or focusing knobs. Keep it away from wet areas and bench edges.

steps.title: Prepare the slide
steps.text: Place a clean prepared slide on the stage and secure it with the slide holder. Keep the specimen centered over the opening and avoid pressing on the coverslip.

steps.title: Select the lowest-power objective
steps.text: Rotate the nosepiece until the lowest-power objective clicks into position. Check that the objective is aligned above the slide before focusing.
steps.warning: Avoid allowing an objective lens to strike the slide. Use the coarse focus only with low power unless your institution's microscope instructions say otherwise.

steps.title: Adjust illumination and find focus
steps.text: Switch on the illuminator and adjust brightness or the diaphragm for a clear field. While viewing from the side, bring the objective close to the slide without touching it; then look through the eyepiece and use the coarse focus slowly to find the image.

steps.title: Sharpen the image and increase magnification
steps.text: Use the fine focus knob to sharpen the specimen. Center the area of interest before rotating to a higher-power objective. At higher magnification, use fine focus for small adjustments.
steps.warning: At high magnification, do not use the coarse focus knob unless the microscope's manufacturer instructions explicitly permit it.

steps.title: Finish and clean up
steps.text: Return to the lowest-power objective, lower the stage, remove the slide and switch off the illuminator. Clean lenses only with approved lens paper and store the microscope covered.

quiz.q: Which objective should be selected first?
quiz.why: Starting at low power makes it easier to locate the specimen and reduces the risk of striking the slide.

quiz.q: Which knob makes small focusing adjustments?
quiz.why: The fine focus knob makes small movements to sharpen the image.

quiz.q: How should a microscope be carried?
options: With one hand on the arm and one under the base
quiz.why: Supporting both the arm and base keeps the microscope stable while carrying it.

quiz.q: What should be used to clean an objective lens?
quiz.why: Lens paper is designed to clean optical surfaces without scratching them.

name: Bunsen burner
purpose: Produces a controllable gas flame for heating and sterilisation tasks where permitted. Use only in a designated area with appropriate supervision and ventilation.

parts.label: Barrel
parts.info: Metal tube through which the gas-air mixture travels and burns at the top.

parts.label: Air collar
parts.info: Rotating sleeve that adjusts the air openings and flame characteristics.

parts.label: Air holes
parts.info: Openings that admit air into the gas stream.

parts.label: Gas control valve
parts.info: Controls gas flow on some burner designs; the bench tap is the main isolation point.

parts.label: Base
parts.info: Supports the burner upright on the bench.

steps.title: Prepare the work area
steps.text: Tie back long hair, secure loose clothing, clear flammable materials and place the burner on a stable, heat-resistant surface. Wear required eye protection and keep a suitable fire blanket or extinguisher accessible.
steps.warning: Never light a burner near flammable solvents, paper, loose hair or clothing. Work only in an approved, supervised laboratory area.

steps.title: Inspect the burner and gas hose
steps.text: Check that the burner, hose and connections are intact and that the air holes are clear. Confirm that the gas tap is off before connecting or inspecting the setup. Report suspected leaks; do not test for leaks with a flame.
steps.warning: If you smell gas or suspect a leak, do not ignite the burner or operate electrical switches. Turn off the gas if safe, alert the supervisor and follow the laboratory emergency procedure.

steps.title: Connect and position the burner
steps.text: Connect the hose securely to the approved gas outlet and burner inlet. Keep the hose away from the flame and hot surfaces. Position the burner upright and check that the area above it is clear.

steps.title: Ignite using the approved procedure
steps.text: Follow your laboratory's ignition sequence and your instructor's direction. Use an approved striker; do not lean over the barrel. Keep the air collar mostly closed for the initial lighting procedure if that is the local protocol.
steps.warning: Light the burner only under direct supervision and using the institution's approved procedure. Keep your face, hands and clothing away from the barrel opening.

steps.title: Adjust the flame and perform the task
steps.text: Once lit, adjust the air collar gradually to obtain the flame specified by your procedure. Keep the burner attended, use appropriate tongs or heat-resistant tools and assume heated objects remain hot after the flame is off.
steps.warning: Never leave a lit burner unattended. Do not reach across a flame, and do not heat sealed containers.

steps.title: Shut down and allow cooling
steps.text: Turn off the gas at the designated bench tap according to local procedure. Confirm the flame is fully extinguished, allow the burner and heated equipment to cool, then disconnect or store equipment as instructed.

quiz.q: What should you do if you suspect a gas leak?
options: Use a flame to find it
Do not ignite; alert the supervisor and follow emergency procedure
quiz.why: A suspected leak is an immediate hazard. Do not ignite or operate switches; follow the laboratory emergency procedure.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the air collar?
quiz.why: The collar changes the air admitted to the gas stream and therefore affects combustion and flame appearance.

quiz.q: Can a lit Bunsen burner be left unattended?
quiz.why: A lit burner must never be left unattended because it can ignite nearby materials or cause burns.

quiz.q: What is the safest way to ignite a burner?
options: Use an approved striker and the local supervised procedure
Lean over the barrel with a match
quiz.why: Use the institution's approved ignition sequence and an approved striker under supervision.
